title: Wendell and the Alibi
premise: Silas Villalobos, an insurance investigator whose photographic memory has made them the unofficial archivist of the small town of Marrow Bend, is pulled into a murder investigation when the victim is found wearing clothes stolen from Silas's own closet—a message meant for them alone. As Sheriff Dane Okonkwo's official inquiry stalls, Silas realizes the killer is someone who once had access to their private case files, someone they trusted with the town's buried secrets. The trail leads to a decade-old fire, an insurance payout that never reached its rightful heirs, and a web of neighbors who benefited from Silas's silence. In the end, Silas must choose between protecting the town's fragile loyalties and exposing the truth: they bait the killer with a falsified file, unmasking Deputy Corliss Ashe—the one person who helped them build the archive—and then burn the files themselves, choosing living people over paper justice.
about_author: Ulyana Thornbury is the pen name of a former claims adjuster who spent eleven years reading other people's disasters for a living before turning them into fiction. They write mysteries from a farmhouse in upstate New York, where they keep meticulous notes and trust almost no one.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of Small Towns
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. We meet Marrow Bend through Silas's filing system—every resident cross-referenced, every secret indexed. A routine claim about a flooded basement reveals the town's quiet dependence on Silas's discretion. Emotional beat: comfort in invisibility, faintly claustrophobic.

chapters.title: Clothes That Weren't Mine
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Called to the old tannery at dawn, Silas recognizes the dead man's jacket instantly—it was stolen from their closet three days ago. Sheriff Okonkwo arrives; Silas hides the recognition. Beat: dread blooming under practiced calm.

chapters.title: Witness, Reluctant
chapters.summary: Sheriff Okonkwo's POV. Okonkwo interviews Silas, sensing evasion but unable to prove it. The victim is identified as Tomas Reyes, a drifter with no local ties—which makes the personal clothing detail stranger. Beat: professional suspicion taking root.

chapters.title: The Missing Hanger
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas returns home to find exactly which garments were taken: the ones worn in a photograph from ten years ago, the night of the Hollis Mill fire. Someone remembers what Silas has tried to forget. Beat: vertigo—the past reaching forward.

chapters.title: Files Under Lock
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas audits their private archive and finds pages subtly reordered—someone has been inside the files, reading them the way only Silas reads them. Beat: violation; the archive was armor, now it's a map.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Ash
chapters.summary: Silas's POV, with flashback. The Hollis Mill fire killed Ruth Hollis; the insurance payout vanished into probate. Silas helped settle it, and helped bury the irregularities. Beat: guilt surfacing like a body in water.

chapters.title: The Deputy Who Reads
chapters.summary: Deputy Corliss Ashe's POV. Corliss, charming and ambitious, offers to help Silas 'informally.' Silas notes Corliss's suspicious fluency with investigative procedure. Beat: warmth with a hairline crack running through it.

chapters.title: What the Widow Kept
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas visits Ruth Hollis's sister, Ada Quintero, who reveals the payout should have gone to her—and that someone in town blocked it. She names no names. Beat: first thread pulled; the town's kindness revealed as complicity.

chapters.title: Second Body, Same Closet
chapters.summary: Okonkwo's POV. A second victim, dressed again in items traced to Silas's home. Okonkwo can no longer treat Silas as bystander and demands full cooperation. Beat: the walls closing in from both sides.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Firelight
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Okonkwo presses Silas about the fire decade; Silas gives truth in fragments, protecting sources. Okonkwo begins to suspect the whole town is lying in chorus. Beat: two careful people circling each other.

chapters.title: The Archive's Blind Spot
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas realizes whoever rearranged the files exploited the one gap in their memory: a week ten years ago when Silas was hospitalized after a car crash. Seven days unaccounted for. Beat: horror at one's own fallibility.

chapters.title: Ada's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ada Quintero's POV. Ada shows Silas her own records—decades of payments funneled through the town council to buy silence about unsafe mill conditions. Everyone signed. Beat: the rot is communal, not singular.

chapters.title: A Note in My Handwriting
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. A threatening note appears, written in an imitation of Silas's hand, warning them off. Only someone who studied the archive could mimic the phrasing habits. Beat: the killer speaking Silas's language back at them.

chapters.title: Corliss at the Window
chapters.summary: Corliss's POV. Corliss watches Silas's house at night, ostensibly on patrol, and we see them pocket something from Silas's porch. Ambiguity deepens—is Corliss protector or predator? Beat: reader doubt weaponized.

chapters.title: The Hospital Week
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas reconstructs the missing week through visitor logs and a nurse's recollection: someone visited repeatedly, someone who claimed to be family. The signature on the log is forged—but familiar. Beat: memory as crime scene.

chapters.title: Town Meeting, Closed Doors
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The town's elders convene secretly about the murders; Silas eavesdrops. They fear exposure of the mill conspiracy more than the killer. Beat: loyalty revealed as blackmail's gentler name.

chapters.title: What Okonkwo Knows
chapters.summary: Okonkwo's POV. Okonkwo shares an off-the-record finding: both victims were witnesses to the mill fire's true cause—arson, not accident. He asks Silas directly: who else knew? Beat: alliance forming across distrust.

chapters.title: The Third Garment
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. A third item from Silas's closet appears, planted in Ada Quintero's shed—framing her. Silas must choose: let Ada take the fall or reveal their own secrets to clear her. Beat: loyalty vs. truth made literal.

chapters.title: Confession, Partial
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas tells Okonkwo about the archive, the fire settlement, everything except the identity they're beginning to suspect. Okonkwo, bound by law, warns this could destroy them both. Beat: relief and terror braided together.

chapters.title: Burning the Middle Drawer
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Someone breaks in and burns a section of the archive—the fire-era files. Silas watches ten years of order go up in smoke and understands: the killer isn't hiding evidence, they're erasing Silas's version of history. Beat: grief for paper, fear for flesh.

chapters.title: Ada Disappears
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, final entry. Ada, frightened, decides to leave town with her ledger—and never arrives anywhere. Her abandoned car is found at the county line. Beat: cold dread; the stakes turn mortal.

chapters.title: Every Road Out
chapters.summary: Okonkwo's POV. Roadblocks, canvassing, nothing. Okonkwo notices the search patterns mirror a training exercise from the state academy—someone policing the police. Beat: the hunter realizing the hunt is choreographed.

chapters.title: The Forged Signature
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas matches the hospital log forgery to documents Corliss once 'helpfully' transcribed for the archive. The suspicion crystallizes—but Silas's evidence burned, and accusing Corliss means accusing their own judgment. Beat: betrayal recognized, still deniable.

chapters.title: Dinner with the Deputy
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas accepts Corliss's dinner invitation, playing oblivious while testing them with deliberate false details about the case. Corliss corrects one—only one—too precisely. Beat: a duel fought entirely in subtext.

chapters.title: What Ruth Saw
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Digging into Ruth Hollis's final days, Silas finds she'd discovered the arson and planned to testify; her death preceded the fire's official ruling. The conspiracy wasn't covering an accident—it was covering a murder. Beat: the case inverts.

chapters.title: Okonkwo's Badge on the Table
chapters.summary: Okonkwo's POV. Okonkwo, stonewalled by the council and state investigators, offers Silas a devil's bargain: work outside the law with him watching, or watch the killer walk. Beat: justice outside the law becomes policy.

chapters.title: The Trap Is Baited
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas fabricates a new archive page—a fake confession naming a fictional accomplice to the arson—and lets it 'leak' through channels only the archive-reader would follow. Beat: turning the killer's obsession into a leash.

chapters.title: Night Watch
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Silas and Okonkwo stake out the archive's hidden duplicate. Hours of tension; near-misses; a figure approaches and slips away, leaving the bait untouched—but a chalk mark on the door, a signal meant for Silas. Beat: dread sharpening into intimacy of threat.

chapters.title: The Chalk Marks
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Deciphering the marks, Silas finds they reference archive notation codes—codes taught to exactly one person years ago. The last rational doubt collapses. Beat: heartbreak arriving ahead of proof.

chapters.title: Confrontation Deferred
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas confronts Corliss obliquely over coffee; Corliss denies everything beautifully and warns Silas that exposing the mill conspiracy will gut the town—pensions, families, graves. 'You'd trade belonging for a filing cabinet?' Beat: the theme stated as temptation.

chapters.title: Where Ada Is
chapters.summary: Okonkwo's POV. Following fuel purchases and a cabin lease, Okonkwo locates Ada alive but captive—kept as insurance against the ledger. He must wait; moving early loses her. Beat: helplessness of the lawful man.

chapters.title: The Killer's File on Me
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas discovers Corliss has built a mirror-archive—a dossier on Silas, every weakness catalogued with loving precision. Reading it, Silas understands they were chosen long ago: Corliss wants Silas to be the final witness who stays silent, forever. Beat: being seen completely, and it's terrible.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. A storm cuts the town off; power fails. Corliss moves, using the blackout. Ada's cabin goes dark on Okonkwo's monitor. Everything converges on one night. Beat: held breath.

chapters.title: The Tannery Again
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. A message lures Silas to the tannery where it began. Corliss awaits, calm, armed, and articulate—arguing that Silas taught them everything, including that truth is just well-organized fiction. Beat: the antagonist's philosophy given its full, seductive hearing.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Price
chapters.summary: Climax part one. Corliss forces Silas to choose: burn the real ledger implicating the town, or Ada dies. Silas appears to comply—then reveals the 'ledger' is the fabricated trap document, and Okonkwo's team closes in. Beat: truth wielded as a weapon.

chapters.title: Fire, Third Time
chapters.summary: Climax part two. Corliss, cornered, sets the tannery alight to destroy everything. Silas goes in for Ada against all sense; Okonkwo pulls them both out as Corliss flees into the storm. Beat: sacrifice answering the book's central question.

chapters.title: Caught in the Open
chapters.summary: Okonkwo's POV. The manhunt ends at the flooded creek crossing—Corliss, soaked and finally ordinary-looking, surrenders without drama. The banality lands harder than any struggle would have. Beat: deflation as catharsis.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas testifies fully—about the fire, the payouts, their own complicity in burying it. The town listens in hostile silence; some thank them later in private, most don't. Beat: truth costs exactly what it promised to.

chapters.title: Ashes Sorted by Hand
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas sorts the remains of the burned archive, keeping only names of the living who deserve restitution, and mails copies to the state attorney general. The system of secrets is dismantled by its own architect. Beat: mourning and release entwined.

chapters.title: A Town With One Fewer Secret
chapters.summary: Silas's POV, epilogue. Months later: Ada rebuilding, Okonkwo re-elected on an honesty platform he half-deserves, Silas keeping a single notebook now—one page per person, mostly blank. Belonging, Silas learns, survives honesty; it just looks different afterward. Final beat: quiet, earned peace.
